open_points.subject: owner-session expiry
open_points.text: “The session ends at the first of: 8 hours after sign-in; 30 minutes without an owner request” but “the pass alone ends sessions by their limits” and the pass runs only every 60 seconds.
open_points.question: Does a session legally end at the limit with deletion deferred to the next pass, or does it end only when the pass processes it?
options: It ends at the limit and remains as an invalid record awaiting deletion
It remains live but unusable until the pass ends it
The pass is deemed to end it retroactively at the limit
open_points.default_guess: It becomes invalid at the limit and is physically removed by the next pass.

open_points.subject: expiry pass versus an admitted owner request
open_points.text: “a request that passes it completes even if a limit or a sign-out comes while it runs” and “the pass alone ends sessions by their limits, taking the import lock and then each session's lock” do not say what happens when the pass ends the session after the request passes the session check but before that request acquires the session lock or changes session state.
open_points.question: May the admitted request still complete, including creating a confirmation or upload, after the expiry pass has removed its session?
options: The admitted request completes and the pass must wait for it
The pass removes the session and the request is refused when it later takes the lock
Store changes may complete but session-state changes may not
open_points.default_guess: Admission and the request's completion should exclude the expiry pass, so every request that passed the check completes before the session can be removed.

open_points.subject: last-request instant
open_points.text: “An owner request is any request to the owner interface that carries the valid session, whatever its answer; its arrival restarts the 30 minutes — of concurrent requests the latest arrival counts” while only “requests ... that change its state” are said to take the session lock.
open_points.question: How is the last-request instant updated atomically for read-only, refused and concurrent requests, and how is that update ordered against the expiry pass?
options: Every request briefly takes the session lock at admission
The instant is an atomic maximum of arrival instants without the session lock
Only the listed session-changing requests update it
open_points.default_guess: Every valid request atomically sets the instant to the maximum of its current value and the captured arrival instant before the request is admitted.

open_points.subject: 60-second expiry pass
open_points.text: “a pass over the sessions it makes every 60 seconds from the start” does not say whether the first pass occurs at startup or 60 seconds later, or what happens to missed pass times while the host is suspended.
open_points.question: When is the first pass, and after suspension does Registry run one pass immediately, replay every missed pass, or wait until the next cadence point?
options: First at startup; one immediate pass after suspension
First after 60 seconds; one immediate overdue pass after suspension
First after 60 seconds; wait for the next future cadence point
Replay every missed pass
open_points.default_guess: Run the first pass 60 seconds after startup and run one overdue pass immediately after resumption.

open_points.subject: expiry-pass locking
open_points.text: “the pass alone ends sessions by their limits, taking the import lock and then each session's lock” does not state whether one import-lock acquisition covers the whole pass or whether it is acquired and released separately for each session.
open_points.question: What is the lock scope of an expiry pass over multiple sessions?
options: Hold the import lock for the entire pass, taking session locks one by one
Acquire and release the import lock with each session lock
Take the import lock only for sessions that hold an uploaded file
open_points.default_guess: Hold the import lock for the whole pass and take each session lock in turn.

open_points.subject: host suspension semantics
open_points.text: The clock “counts the time the host or its VM was suspended, so a session does not outlive a suspension”. Counting suspended time expires only sessions whose limit is reached during the suspension; a short suspension can leave a session valid.
open_points.question: Does every host or VM suspension end every owner session, or does suspension merely consume the ordinary 8-hour and 30-minute durations?
options: Every suspension ends every session
Suspended time counts, but a session survives when neither limit is reached
Only suspension of at least 30 minutes ends an otherwise idle session
open_points.default_guess: Suspended time consumes the ordinary durations; suspension itself is not a separate ending event.

open_points.subject: backup scheduler polling
open_points.text: “The process looks at the clock at least once a minute” does not identify whether that one-minute interval is measured by wall-clock time, a suspend-counting monotonic clock, or another clock.
open_points.question: What clock and maximum interval govern scheduler looks, especially across wall-clock changes and host suspension?
options: At most 60 suspend-counting monotonic seconds between looks
At least once in each UTC wall-clock minute
At most 60 monotonic seconds excluding suspension between looks
open_points.default_guess: Use a suspend-counting monotonic interval of at most 60 seconds, reading UTC wall time at each look.

open_points.subject: backup encryption
open_points.text: “Each backup is encrypted with the backup key” does not declare the encryption construction, authentication requirement, nonce generation, key derivation or ciphertext format.
open_points.question: What exact authenticated-encryption scheme and key-handling rules must every implementation use so that independently written implementations create and verify the same protected backup format?
options: A specified AEAD with a random nonce and the configured bytes as its key
A specified AEAD with a KDF deriving its key from the configured value
Implementation-selected authenticated encryption
Encryption without authenticated integrity
open_points.default_guess: Specify a versioned AEAD format with a fresh operating-system-random nonce and a defined KDF from the configured backup key.

open_points.subject: backup key digest
open_points.text: A backup records “a digest of the key it was made with (never the key)” but no digest algorithm, encoding, domain separation or comparison rule is stated.
open_points.question: How is the key digest computed and validated, and is it intended only as a key identifier or as a security check?
options: A fixed unkeyed cryptographic hash of the configured key
A fixed KDF-derived key identifier with domain separation
A random key identifier stored separately from the key
An implementation-selected digest
open_points.default_guess: Use a fixed domain-separated cryptographic key identifier and verify it against the configured key during creation checks.

open_points.subject: unencrypted backup record
open_points.text: The backup “records, readable without its key” its metadata, while a kept record is valid merely “when its instant, release, last sequence number and key digest can all be read”. The text does not say that this unencrypted record is authenticated by the encrypted content or exactly which values and ranges count as readable.
open_points.question: Must the plaintext record be cryptographically authenticated and matched against the decrypted backup, and what validation makes each metadata field valid rather than merely parseable?
options: Authenticate all metadata as AEAD associated data and compare it with values inside the decrypted store
Put an authenticated copy inside the ciphertext and compare both copies
Leave metadata unauthenticated and accept any parseable values
open_points.default_guess: Authenticate the complete metadata as associated data and verify the release, sequence and key identifier against the decrypted backup.

open_points.subject: newest-backup owner view during a run
open_points.text: “The owner interface shows the instant of the newest kept backup whose record can be read” does not order that read against temporary cleanup, retention deletion and the rename that makes a new backup kept.
open_points.question: What may the owner view return when it races a backup run that is deleting or renaming backup files?
options: Serialize the view with the whole backup run
Return a consistent filesystem snapshot from either before or after the relevant rename/deletions
Permit transient omission or file-read failures
open_points.default_guess: Return a consistent before-or-after view and never expose a transient file error.
